AbstractText: Triamcinolone (T) is a glucocorticoid commonly used to relieve inflammation and treat arthritis, severe allergies and asthma; however, it is banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency in competition for athletes when administered orally, intravenously, intramuscularly, or rectally. The minimum required performance limit (MRPL) for urinary T is 30 ng/mL. However, the data about the urinary excretion of T after oral administration is limited. We aimed to investigate the elimination profile and determine whether single-dose administration of T would cause a positive doping result.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Twelve healthy volunteers received a single-dose of 4-mg T orally, and urine samples were collected for 24 h. A validated liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method was used to determine urinary T levels. Non-compartmental modeling was used to estimate the pharmacokinetic parameters.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: All the urinary T concentrations were much higher than the MRPL. The peak urinary T concentration was 3211.4 ± 860.3 ng/mL (mean ± SD), time to peak concentration was 1.7 ± 0.9 h, and the estimated elimination half-life was 4.4 ± 2.8 h. About 27.76% of the consumed dose was eliminated via urine within 24 h after intake.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: After a single-dose oral administration, urinary T concentrations still exceeded the MRPL after 24 h. This information could be useful for limiting the misuse of T. Athletes should be aware when using T in competition and acquire approval for a therapeutic use exemption prior to use. Moreover, the elimination profile of orally administered T may be crucial information for distinguishing different dosage routes.
